editorial:
You get a tense legal thriller built around one bad night and a guilty conscience. Mitch Brockden is a rising district attorney who accidentally hits a man and runs. When Clinton Davis is blamed, Mitch uses his power to get him off, thinking he is fixing a mistake. Instead, he frees a dangerous killer. The movie keeps you watching because every choice Mitch makes digs him deeper, and Samuel L. Jackson brings quiet menace to Clinton. It is not a huge-budget spectacle, but it moves fast and keeps the stakes personal.

The best parts are the cat-and-mouse tension and the way Mitch's panic grows as the truth comes out. The courtroom scenes are simple, and some twists feel a little too convenient, but the story stays easy to follow. If you like crime thrillers with moral gray areas, this is a solid weekend pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the sharpest picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Mitch learns Clinton is the real killer and that the man Mitch hit was already dead. Clinton targets Mitch's family, forcing a violent showdown. Mitch fights back, kills Clinton, and survives, but his career and conscience are left badly damaged.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves crime thrillers with moral gray areas.
